scene_translation: Using the map in the old notebook as a guide, Tesuto stepped into the dim underground passage. The air was cold, and faint wartime graffiti still remained on the concrete walls. After walking for a while, the man in the grey coat was there, leaning against the wall, waiting. "You came, Tesuto. Beyond this point, you won't manage alone," he said, pointing to an iron door deep in the passage.
grammar_note: 【おまえ】A blunt, rough second-person pronoun used by older or gruff men — it's not quite rude but signals the speaker sees himself as superior or close. Compare: あなた (polite/neutral), きみ (soft/casual), おまえ (rough, familiar). The grey man has dropped any pretense of distance.

mystery_memo: Scene 8: Tesuto has entered the wartime underground passage beneath Shinjuku using the notebook map. The grey man was waiting — this confirms he has been guiding the player deliberately, not simply following. He knows Tesuto's name and seems to have been here before. The iron door ahead likely requires the coin locker key (from scene 4). The graffiti on the walls may hold further clues about the grandmother's wartime past. The woman in blue has not appeared here yet — her absence is notable. NPC relationships: shopkeeper (frightened/closed off), bartender (quietly helpful), shrine priest (formally cryptic), grey man (shifting from antagonist to reluctant guide — now clearly an ally with his own agenda). The お守り from the shrine may have protective or symbolic significance in the revelation ahead.
